3. Appellant pre-emptees 1.5 contested the case by filing a joint written objection denying the allegations of the pre-emptor respondents 1-3. Their case is that the application for pre-emption is barred by limitation as they knew about the transfer from the very beginning. The case land was inherited by Barada Prasad's three sons, namely, Jyoti Prasad, Tarun Tapan & Netra Ranjan. Netra Ranjan died leaving his two brothers Jyoti Prasad and Tarun Tapan as his only heirs. Pre-emptor respondent No. 1 Mohammad Islam was the karja karak, of Jyoti Prasad & Tarun. He was the caretaker of the case land for the vendors. When the vendors wanted to sell the case land, none of the co-sharers including the three pre-emptors agreed to purchase the same. Pre-emptor respondent No.1 then requested the appellant pre-emptees 1.5 to purchase the case land stating that he did not have money to purchase the land. Pre-emptor respondent No. 1 settled the price of the case land and was present at the time of registration of the disputed kabala dated 27.4.79. He also delivered possession of the case land to the pre-emptee purchasers on behalf of the vendors. Pre-emptee purchasers gave notices to all co-sharers and Paid rents to the Government. Subsequent to the present purchase pre-emptee Respondent No. 3 Gera Mia (O.P.W. 1) became co-sharer in the case land by purchase by a kabala dated 25.8.79 (Ext. A). The pre-emptees 1.4 did not possess the case land as bargadars under the vendors. After the purchase of the case land the pre-emptees built a salt godown in a portion of the case land. The story that the pre-emptors came.to know about the purchase of the case land by the pre-emptees from P.W. 2 Ufa Mia on 16.6.81 and that the pre-emptees possessed the case land from before the purchase under the vendors is not true. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge believed the evidence of pre-emptor P.W. 1 Mohammad Islam that 'the pre-emptors who were non-notified co-sharers came to know about the transfer for the first time on 16.6.81, that he case land used to be possessed by the pre-emptee purchasers 1-4 as bargadars from before their purchase, that the case is not barred by limitation and that the petitioners were entitled in law to Pre-empt the case land. On these findings he allowed the prayer of the pre-emptors with costs. There after the pre-emptees 1-5 have preferred this appeal. 

 18. Section 141 C.P.C. provides that the procedure provided in the C.P.C. in regard to suits shall be followed, as far as it can be made applicable, in all proceedings in any Court of Civil jurisdiction. The above quoted provisions of Orders 8 and 14 there-fore apply to the present proceeding. As already stated, the pre-emptees in the instant case gave general denial but did not specifically deny the assertion of the pre-emptors regarding the question of maximum ceiling of land and did not specifically allege that if the pre-emption application is allowed, the added land would exceed the permissible limit. Therefore it is not a sufficient denial in terms of Order 8 rule 3 C.P.C. The rule in Order 8, rule 5 is known as the doctrine of non-traverse which means that where a material averment is passed over by evasive denial without a specific denial, it is taken to admitted. Thus the material proposition of fact affirmed by the pre-emptors regarding the fact that if the pre-emption is allowed, the added land will not exceed the ceiling of land the pre-emptor are permitted to hold under the law has not been specifically and sufficiently denied by the pre-emptees. Therefore in terms of rule 1 (1) and rule 1 (3) of Order 14 C.P.C. there was no issue before the trial Court nor this Court is required to give any finding in respect of ceiling of land in the absence of any specific averment to the contrary. There is thus no substance in the argument of the learned Advocate for the pre-emptees that the application for pre-emption is liable to be rejected as the pre-emptors did not adduce any evidence in support of their assertion regarding the ceiling of land because, as already stated, there is absence of specific averment to the Contrary. In this connection a reference may be made to the decision in, the case of Md. Matiur Rahman Vs. Md. Iman Ali @ Md. Iman Miah & others, 1981 B.L. D. (A.D.) . 280 Wherein it has been held that mere omission to make an assertion in respect of ceiling of land in the application by the pre-emptors, or to adduce evidence to this effect in the absence of any averment to the contrary wily not render the application liable to be dismissed and  record a finding to this effect in such a Stance cannot be a ground for dismissal of the pre-emption case. 

 19. There is no specific allegation in the instant case in the written objection filed before the. trial Court that any co-sharer has not been in the application. Objection as to omission of a necessary party must be taken at the earliest opportunity and if no such objection in respect of non-joinder of parties is taken; it may be deemed that objection regarding omission of necessary party has: been waived.
